To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

boundary-spanners in global IS projects mediate the transfer of knowledge across different domains by (1) creating and communicating knowledge objects, (2) building and maintaining social networks of practice, and (3) managing the knowledge boundaries between different domains.

the boundary spanners in the IS change projects were able to broker and embed organizational knowledge in the social network structure of the project by: (1) defining the project as a knowledge domain boundary, (2) legitimizing their own knowledge as a form of expertise, (3) communicating knowledge across the virtual network of practice, (4) selecting the boundary-spanners, and (5) mediating the different forms of knowledge-domain boundaries.
the boundary-spanning role is not a single role that is filled by the same people in all projects, but rather a set of roles that are played by different people in different projects.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how knowledge is brokered in the social networks of boundary-spanning projects.

how the social networks of boundary-spanning projects are constructed, how knowledge is mediated and embedded in the network, and how this knowledge becomes embedded in the organizational routines and practices of a global consultancy firm.
the social processes through which knowledge becomes embedded in the organizational structure and the implications for the management of IS change projects in global organizations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this paper contributes to the understanding of knowledge mediation and boundary spanning in global IS change projects.
the study has provided a better understanding of the knowledge mediation process and the boundary-spanning roles of the change agents.
the boundary-spanners are the ones who are able to mediate between different forms of knowledge, and that they are able to do so by using the various knowledge brokering mechanisms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the knowledge of the project team members is a critical success factor for the project.
the knowledge of the organization is mediated and embedded in the social networks that span the boundaries of different communities of practice.
we have developed a model for the knowledge mediation process in global IS change projects, which can be applied in a variety of organizational contexts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
boundary-spanners play a crucial role in the mediation of organizational knowledge, and that this mediation is not a simple matter of transferring knowledge across organizational boundaries.
knowledge is not a commodity that can be easily transferred across organizational boundaries, but rather a social construct that is shaped by the social networks of boundary-spanning agents.

boundary-spanning is a highly social process, involving the active construction, negotiation, and communication of different kinds of knowledge, as well as the development of social networks of practice across organizational domains.
